# dsh-hogwarts-loop
中文
**Plan → build → review → commit, as a DeepSeek Harness plugin.** One subagent per cast member, each
dispatched on **its own configurable model**.
`@dyikai/dsh-hogwarts-loop` packages the `hogwarts-loop` discipline: take a large engineering effort
from a plan to reviewed, committed code in small, independently verified checkpoints. The methodolo
gy ships as a skill, every cast member is a managed subagent started through one tool, and the model
behind each role is set in the client instead of being baked into the prompt.
## What it adds

d` |
| Create or continue the same cast member within a parent session | the `hogwarts_dispatch` too

l | registered by `index.js` |

Hogwarts Loop**, plus the Plugins page row for this plugin | `client.js` (browser half) |

**One parent session, one child per role.** Checkpoints and fix rounds keep the same `childId`; chan
ging `description`, completing a CP, or becoming inactive does not create a new Harry. Each role is
independent, so Harry and Severus retain separate histories. Dispatch is nonblocking: wait for a rol
e's report before assigning its next CP; concurrent calls to that role do not create parallel worker
s report before assigning its next CP; concurrent calls to that role do not create parallel workers.
Bindings survive plugin reload and resuming the same parent session. A continuation failure never si
lently creates a replacement. Older histories with ambiguous role bindings require intervention inst
ead of guessing. A genuinely new parent session starts its own cast, rehydrated from the plan.
Results distinguish `started` from `continued`. Creation reports the configured provider/model; cont
inuation identifies the existing child rather than claiming it uses newly edited defaults. `cwd` is
creation-only: a non-empty `cwd` on a later call is rejected. Omit it to preserve the child's establ
ished working directory. The roster label keeps the first `description`; later briefs do not relabel
ng directory. The roster label keeps the first `description`; later briefs do not relabel the child.
## Conditional ablation

The skill requires a complexity report on every Harry delivery. When the
ablation policy triggers, H

removal/substitution experiments without weakening acceptance, verifies the
com

bined survivor, and gives Severus the evidence to audit. This is a workflow
gate, not a runtime code

-size scanner; direct manual dispatch skips the skill's
checkpoint discipline. Thresholds and counti
ng rules have one canonical home.
## Review discipline

The review contract keeps a few rules:
validate blocking candidates before repair, preserve evidence

and finding IDs,
and independently check the fix rather than repeating the whole review.
Complete r

epair/re-review rounds and evidence-only batches have separate budgets;
normal proof gathering is no

t counted as another repair round. Eligible same-root
advisor-guided diagnosis or implementation has

a narrow precedence rule, without
a code-edit prerequisite; it is not a budget reset or exemption f

or blind probe
churn or unrelated work (see Escalation below).

One reviewer is the default. Specialists cover an actual changed risk or unresolved
question, not ev

ery file in a broad category. Required human approvals remain in
force. These are workflow instructi
ons, not host permissions or runtime enforcement.

Evaluation distinguishes fixture checks from real
before/after review comparisons. A repository-deri

ved pair and repair replay
complements the synthetic cases; scoring and provenance
stay outside revi
ewer context. None of these artifacts is a model-quality score.

Working plans, progress lists and review reports stay in the session or task-scoped
temporary storag

e by default, not in Git or behind `.gitignore`. Only an explicitly
approved, maintained roadmap/des

ign document is durable; the shipped plan template

## Install
Requires Node.js ≥ 20 and a DeepSeek Harness profile.
### From the Add plugin wizard
Type `@dyikai/dsh-hogwarts-loop` into the **Add plugin** wizard's search box and click **Install**.
### Why the form looks like this
- The form registers twice — in the settings panel's `settings.section` and in the Plugins page's `p
lugins.row.config` (key `@dyikai/dsh-hogwarts-loop#hogwarts-loop`) — and both render the same `FormB

ody`.
- The settings-panel entry resolves this plugin's namespace through the shared `settings.descr
ibe` mirror (matching the `hogwarts-loop` suffix, so an `include:` prefix still works) and then gets
a version-fenced write handle via `ctx.configForms.get(ns)`. The Plugins entry receives the bound `

form` directly from the page, so it never has to guess a namespace.
- On the host side, `Config` mar
ks the two top-level objects `delegation` and `roles` as `.volatile()` (schemastery cannot nest vola
tile, so the reference has to sit on the object). That is both what makes the settings service treat
the entry as editable and serve the settings panel, and what guarantees new role creation reads the

**current** defaults rather than a snapshot taken when the plugin activated.
- When the model catal
og cannot be read (expired login, failed catalog request), the same fields fall back to text inputs

instead of breaking the page.
- A wrong creation-time model is never a silent failure: `hogwarts_dis
patch` validates the route before creating a role and returns an actionable tool error.
